The proposed update is a gated residual mechanism with established precedents. [Highway Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.00387) use H(h)⊙T(h)+h⊙(1−T(h)); here the identity path stays ungated and only the residual u is scaled. [WaveNet](https://arxiv.org/html/1609.03499v1) multiplies tanh features by sigmoid gates inside residual blocks and supports conditioning through additive projections into gate/filter preactivations. [Gated convolutional networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.08083) use GLUs, A⊙sigmoid(B), making sigmoid modulation of a convolutional update familiar. [FiLM](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.07871) applies conditional feature-wise affine modulation γ(c)⊙u+β(c); the proposed gate resembles restricted, scale-only FiLM with c=[h;u;e_t]. Algebraically, dividing by sigmoid(2) allows scales up to approximately 1.135; zero gate weights and bias 2 recover h+u. These comparisons suggest novelty would require evidence for the specific conditioning design, rather than gating itself.

Explicit e_t supplies a direct route to current-item identity, but no new observed information: h and u already derive from the input sequence. Its possible contribution is easier access to information obscured by deeper transformations. Recommended controls: ordinary h+u; learned constant channel scales; gates using h, u, [h;u], and [h;u;e_t]; and a parameter-matched [h;u] gate with extra capacity or a duplicated/projected hidden-feature branch replacing e_t. Train shuffled-item conditioning controls to test alignment while retaining parameter count and embedding statistics. Match initialization, residual scale, training budget, and evaluation; use seed 42 and macro validation HR@10 across all four categories. Gate saturation and sensitivity to replacing e_t can diagnose usage, but only controlled validation gains support its contribution. Each variant remains one jointly trained NextItNet per category.
